You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

% HEXYL(1) hexyl 0.12.0 | General Commands Manual
%
% 2022-12-05

# NAME

hexyl - a command-line hex viewer

# SYNOPSIS

**hexyl** [_OPTIONS_] [_FILE_]

# DESCRIPTION

**hexyl** is a simple hex viewer for the terminal.
It uses a colored output to distinguish different categories of bytes (NULL
bytes, printable ASCII characters, ASCII whitespace characters, other ASCII
characters and non-ASCII).

# POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS

_FILE_
:   The file to display.
    If no _FILE_ argument is given, read from STDIN.

# OPTIONS

**-n**, **\--length** _N_
:   Only read _N_ bytes from the input.
    The _N_ argument can also include a unit with a decimal prefix (kB, MB, ..)
    or binary prefix (kiB, MiB, ..), or can be specified using a hex number.

    Examples:

    :   

        Read the first 64 bytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=64**

        Read the first 4 kibibytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=4KiB**

        Read the first 255 bytes (specified using a hex number):
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=0xff**

**-c**, **\--bytes** _N_
:   An alias for **-n**/**\--length**.

**-l** _N_
:   Yet another alias for **-n**/**\--length**.

**-s**, **\--skip** _N_
:   Skip the first _N_ bytes of the input.
    The _N_ argument can also include a unit (see **\--length** for details).
    A negative value is valid and will seek from the end of the file.

**\--block-size** _SIZE_
:   Sets the size of the block unit to _SIZE_ (default is 512).

    Examples:

    :   

        Sets the block size to 1024 bytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--block-size=1024 \--length=5block**

        Sets the block size to 4 kilobytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--block-size=4kB \--length=2block**

**-v**, **\--no-squeezing**
:   Displays all input data.
    Otherwise any number of groups of output lines which would be identical to
    the preceding group of lines, are replaced with a line comprised of a
    single asterisk.

**\--color** _WHEN_
:   When to use colors.
    The auto-mode only displays colors if the output goes to an interactive
    terminal.

    Possible values:

    :   - **always** (default)
        - **auto**
        - **never**

**\--border** _STYLE_
:   Whether to draw a border with Unicode characters, ASCII characters, or none
    at all.

    Possible values:

    :   - **unicode** (default)
        - **ascii**
        - **none**

**-o**, **\--display-offset** _N_
:   Add _N_ bytes to the displayed file position.
    The _N_ argument can also include a unit (see **\--length** for details).
    A negative value is valid and calculates an offset relative to the end of
    the file.

**-h**, **\--help**
:   Prints help information.

**-V**, **\--version**
:   Prints version information.

# ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES

**hexyl** colors can be configured via environment variables. The variables used are as follows:

:   - **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_PRINTABLE**: Any non-whitespace printable ASCII character
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_WHITESPACE**: Whitespace such as space or newline (only visible in middle panel with byte values)
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_OTHER**: Any other ASCII character (< **0x80**) besides null
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_NULL**: The null byte (**0x00**)
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_NONASCII**: Any non-ASCII byte (> **0x7F**)
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_OFFSET**: The lefthand file offset

The colors can be any of the 8 standard terminal colors: **black**, **blue**, **cyan**, **green**, **magenta**, **red**,
**yellow** and **white**. The "bright" variants are also supported (e.g., **bright blue**). Additionally, you can use
the RGB hex format, **#abcdef**. For example, **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_PRINTABLE=blue HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_WHITESPACE="bright green"
HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_OTHER="#ff7f99"**.

# NOTES

Source repository:
:   <https://github.com/sharkdp/hexyl>

# EXAMPLES

Print a given file:
:   $ **hexyl small.png**

Print and view a given file in the terminal pager:
:   $ **hexyl big.png | less -r**

Print the first 256 bytes of a given special file:
:   $ **hexyl -n 256 /dev/urandom**

# AUTHORS

**hexyl** was written by David Peter <mail@david-peter.de>.

# REPORTING BUGS

Bugs can be reported on GitHub at:
:   <https://github.com/sharkdp/hexyl/issues>

# COPYRIGHT

**hexyl** is dual-licensed under:

:   - Apache License 2.0 (<https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0>)
    - MIT License (<https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT>)

# SEE ALSO

**hexdump**(1), **xxd**(1)

fn print_long_help() {
    print!("{}", HELP_LONG);
}
fn print_short_help() {
    print!("{}", HELP_SHORT);
}

fn build_command() -> Command {
    Command::new("hexyl")
        .disable_help_flag(true)
        .disable_version_flag(true)
        .arg(Arg::new("FILE").help("The file to display. If no FILE argument is given, read from STDIN"))
        .arg(Arg::new("length").short('n').long("length").alias("bytes").short_alias('c').short_alias('l').value_name("N").help("Only read N bytes"))
        .arg(Arg::new("skip").short('s').long("skip").value_name("N").help("Skip"))
        .arg(Arg::new("block-size").long("block-size").value_name("SIZE").default_value("512").help("block size"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-squeezing").short('v').long("no-squeezing").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("color").long("color").value_name("WHEN").default_value("always").value_parser(value_parser!(String)).help("color"))
        .arg(Arg::new("border").long("border").value_name("STYLE").default_value("unicode").value_parser(value_parser!(String)))
        .arg(Arg::new("plain").short('p').long("plain").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-characters").long("no-characters").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("characters").short('C').long("characters").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("character-table").long("character-table").value_name("FORMAT").default_value("default").value_parser(value_parser!(String)))
        .arg(Arg::new("color-scheme").long("color-scheme").value_name("FORMAT").default_value("default").value_parser(value_parser!(String)))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-position").short('P').long("no-position").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("display-offset").short('o').long("display-offset").value_name("N").default_value("0"))
        .arg(Arg::new("panels").long("panels").value_name("N"))
        .arg(Arg::new("group-size").short('g').long("group-size").alias("groupsize").value_name("N").default_value("1"))
        .arg(Arg::new("endianness").long("endianness").value_name("FORMAT").default_value("big"))
        .arg(Arg::new("e").short('e').action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("base").short('b').long("base").value_name("B").default_value("hexadecimal"))
        .arg(Arg::new("terminal-width").long("terminal-width").value_name("N"))
        .arg(Arg::new("print-color-table").long("print-color-table").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("include").short('i').long("include").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("completion").long("completion").value_name("SHELL"))
        .arg(Arg::new("help_flag").short('h').long("help").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("version_flag").short('V').long("version").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
}

# NAME

hexyl - a command-line hex viewer

# SYNOPSIS

**hexyl** [_OPTIONS_] [_FILE_]

# DESCRIPTION

**hexyl** is a simple hex viewer for the terminal.
It uses a colored output to distinguish different categories of bytes (NULL
bytes, printable ASCII characters, ASCII whitespace characters, other ASCII
characters and non-ASCII).

# POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS

_FILE_
:   The file to display.
    If no _FILE_ argument is given, read from STDIN.

# OPTIONS

**-n**, **\--length** _N_
:   Only read _N_ bytes from the input.
    The _N_ argument can also include a unit with a decimal prefix (kB, MB, ..)
    or binary prefix (kiB, MiB, ..), or can be specified using a hex number.

    Examples:

        :   $ **hexyl \--length=64**

        Read the first 4 kibibytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=4KiB**

        Read the first 255 bytes (specified using a hex number):
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=0xff**

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    // handle help/version early for exact output
    let mut has_long_help = false;
    let mut has_short_help = false;
    let mut has_version = false;
    for a in &args[1..] {
        if a == "--help" { has_long_help = true; }
        else if a == "-h" { has_short_help = true; }
        else if a == "--version" || a == "-V" { has_version = true; }
    }
    // priority: --help overrides -h? original gave long help if both present? test earlier: --help and --version together gave help, but --help alone gives long, -h alone gives short.
    // If both --help and -h present, which to show? clap may show long if --help present. We'll mimic.
    if has_long_help {
        print!("{}", HELP_LONG);
        process::exit(0);
    }
    if has_short_help {
        print!("{}", HELP_SHORT);
        process::exit(0);
    }
    if has_version {
        println!("hexyl {}", VERSION);
        process::exit(0);
    }

    if let Err(e) = run(args) {
        eprintln!("{}", e);
        process::exit( get_exit_code(&e) );
    }
}

fn get_exit_code(msg: &str) -> i32 {
    if msg.starts_with("error:") {
        2
    } else if msg.starts_with("Error:") {
        1
    } else {
        1
    }
}

// parsing structures
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Config {
    length: Option<u64>,
    skip: Option<i64>, // may be negative, but after parsing we have signed
    block_size: u64,
    no_squeezing: bool,
    color: String,
    border: String,
    plain: bool,
    no_characters: bool,
    characters: bool,
    character_table: String,
    color_scheme: String,
    no_position: bool,
    display_offset: u64,
    panels: Option<String>, // None or "auto" or number string
    group_size: u8,
    endianness: String,
    use_e_flag: bool,
    base: String,
    terminal_width: Option<u64>,
    print_color_table: bool,
    include: bool,
    completion: Option<String>,
    file: Option<String>,
    // flags for tracking duplicates
    // we need to track if plain already set etc for error handling - done during parse
}

fn run(args: Vec<String>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let cfg = parse_args(args)?;
    if let Some(shell) = cfg.completion {
        print_completion(&shell)?;
        return Ok(());
    }
    if cfg.print_color_table {
        print_color_table();
        return Ok(());
    }
    if cfg.include {
        return run_include(&cfg);
    }
    // otherwise hex viewing
    run_hex(&cfg)
}

fn print_completion(shell: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let out = match shell {
        "bash" => COMPLETION_BASH,
        "fish" => COMPLETION_FISH,
        "zsh" => COMPLETION_ZSH,
        "powershell" => COMPLETION_POWERSHELL,
        "elvish" => COMPLETION_ELVISH,
        _ => return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--completion <SHELL>'\n  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", shell)),
    };
    print!("{}", out);
    Ok(())
}

fn print_color_table() {
    println!("hexyl color reference:");
    println!();
    println!("\x1b[90m⋄ NULL bytes (0x00)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[36ma ASCII printable characters (0x20 - 0x7E)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[32m_ ASCII whitespace (0x09 - 0x0D, 0x20)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[32m• ASCII control characters (except NULL and whitespace)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[33m× Non-ASCII bytes (0x80 - 0xFF)\x1b[39m");
}

fn parse_args(args: Vec<String>) -> Result<Config, String> {
    let mut cfg = Config {
        length: None,
        skip: None,
        block_size: 512,
        no_squeezing: false,
        color: "always".to_string(),
        border: "unicode".to_string(),
        plain: false,
        no_characters: false,
        characters: false,
        character_table: "default".to_string(),
        color_scheme: "default".to_string(),
        no_position: false,
        display_offset: 0,
        panels: None,
        group_size: 1,
        endianness: "big".to_string(),
        use_e_flag: false,
        base: "hexadecimal".to_string(),
        terminal_width: None,
        print_color_table: false,
        include: false,
        completion: None,
        file: None,
        // ...
    };
    // Track which args have been set for duplicate detection
    let mut seen_length = false;
    let mut seen_skip = false;
    let mut seen_block_size = false;
    let mut seen_no_squeezing = false;
    let mut seen_color = false;
    let mut seen_border = false;
    let mut seen_plain = false;
    let mut seen_no_characters = false;
    let mut seen_characters = false;
    let mut seen_character_table = false;
    let mut seen_color_scheme = false;
    let mut seen_no_position = false;
    let mut seen_display_offset = false;
    let mut seen_panels = false;
    let mut seen_group_size = false;
    let mut seen_endianness = false;
    let mut seen_base = false;
    let mut seen_terminal_width = false;
    let mut seen_print_color_table = false;
    let mut seen_include = false;
    let mut seen_completion = false;

    let mut i = 1;
    let n = args.len();
    let mut positional: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    while i < n {
        let arg = &args[i];
        if arg == "--" {
            // everything after is positional
            for j in i+1..n {
                positional.push(args[j].clone());
            }
            break;
        } else if arg.starts_with("--") {
            // long option
            let (key, val_opt) = if let Some(eq_pos) = arg.find('=') {
                (&arg[..eq_pos], Some(arg[eq_pos+1..].to_string()))
            } else {
                (arg.as_str(), None)
            };
            match key {
                "--length" | "--bytes" => {
                    if seen_length { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--length <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_length = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--length <N>")?;
                    cfg.length = Some(parse_byte_count(&val, cfg.block_size, "--length", false)?);
                }
                "--skip" => {
                    if seen_skip { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--skip <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_skip = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--skip <N>")?;
                    cfg.skip = Some(parse_byte_count_signed(&val, cfg.block_size, "--skip")?);
                }
                "--block-size" => {
                    if seen_block_size { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--block-size <SIZE>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_block_size = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--block-size <SIZE>")?;
                    cfg.block_size = parse_block_size(&val)?;
                }
                "--no-squeezing" => {
                    if seen_no_squeezing { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--no-squeezing' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_no_squeezing = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--no-squeezing' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.no_squeezing = true;
                }
                "--color" => {
                    if seen_color { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--color <WHEN>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_color = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--color <WHEN>")?;
                    if !["always","auto","never","force"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--color <WHEN>'\n  [possible values: always, auto, never, force]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.color = val;
                }
                "--border" => {
                    if seen_border { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--border <STYLE>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_border = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--border <STYLE>")?;
                    if !["unicode","ascii","none"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--border <STYLE>'\n  [possible values: unicode, ascii, none]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.border = val;
                }
                "--plain" => {
                    if seen_plain { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--plain' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_plain = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--plain' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.plain = true;
                }
                "--no-characters" => {
                    if seen_no_characters { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--no-characters' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_no_characters = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--no-characters' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.no_characters = true;
                }
                "--characters" => {
                    if seen_characters { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--characters' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_characters = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--characters' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.characters = true;
                }
                "--character-table" => {
                    if seen_character_table { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--character-table <FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_character_table = true;

fn parse_byte_count(s: &str, block_size: u64, arg_name: &str, allow_negative: bool) -> Result<u64, String> {

    // For skip, negative allowed via parse_byte_count_signed. This function is for positive only.

    if s.starts_with('-') {
        return Err(format!("Error: failed to parse `{}` arg \"{}\" as byte count\n\nCaused by:\n    negative offset specified, but only positive offsets (counts) are accepted in this context\n", arg_name, s));

    parse_byte_count_inner(s, block_size, arg_name)

fn read_input(cfg: &Config) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Option<String>), String> {
    // returns data vector and optional filename (if file source)
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    let mut file_opt: Option<String> = None;
    let mut file_len: Option<u64> = None;

    if let Some(fname) = &cfg.file {
        // open file
        let mut file = File::open(fname).map_err(|e| format!("Error: {} (os error {})", e.to_string(), e.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0)))?;
        // Need file length for negative skip/display offset? But display offset negative not allowed per parse, skip negative handled via seek.
        // For include mode, length already handles limit.
        file_len = file.metadata().ok().map(|m| m.len());
        file_opt = Some(fname.clone());

        // Handle skip
        if let Some(skip_val) = cfg.skip {
            if skip_val >= 0 {
                file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(skip_val as u64)).map_err(|e| format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"))?;
            } else {
                // negative: seek from end
                // skip_val is negative, so -skip_val bytes from end
                let abs = (-skip_val) as u64;
                // Need file len
                if let Some(len) = file_len {
                    if abs > len {
                        return Err(format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"));
                    }
                    file.seek(SeekFrom::End(-(abs as i64))).map_err(|_| format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"))?;
                } else {
                    return Err(format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"));
                }
            }
        }

        // Now read up to length
        if let Some(len) = cfg.length {
            let mut limited = file.take(len);
            limited.read_to_end(&mut data).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        } else {
            file.read_to_end(&mut data).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        }
    } else {
        // stdin
        let stdin = io::stdin();
        let mut handle = stdin.lock();
        // For stdin, skip handling is different: read and discard
        // If skip is negative, error (since not seekable)
        if let Some(skip_val) = cfg.skip {
            if skip_val < 0 {
                return Err(format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"));
            } else {
                // discard skip_val bytes
                let mut remaining = skip_val as u64;
                let mut buf = [0u8; 8192];
                while remaining > 0 {
                    let to_read = std::cmp::min(remaining, buf.len() as u64) as usize;
                    let n = handle.read(&mut buf[..to_read]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                    if n == 0 { break; }
                    remaining -= n as u64;
                }
                // For too large skip beyond EOF, just produce empty output (no error) but our earlier test showed skip too large file gave "No content" with rc 0, while skip -100 too large gave error. So positive skip beyond EOF is not error.
            }
        }
        if let Some(len) = cfg.length {
            let mut limited = handle.take(len);
            limited.read_to_end(&mut data).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        } else {
            handle.read_to_end(&mut data).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        }
    }
    Ok((data, file_opt))
}

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    // handle help/version early for exact output
    let mut has_long_help = false;
    let mut has_short_help = false;
    let mut has_version = false;
    for a in &args[1..] {
        if a == "--help" { has_long_help = true; }
        else if a == "-h" { has_short_help = true; }
        else if a == "--version" || a == "-V" { has_version = true; }
    }
    // priority: --help overrides -h? original gave long help if both present? test earlier: --help and --version together gave help, but --help alone gives long, -h alone gives short.
    // If both --help and -h present, which to show? clap may show long if --help present. We'll mimic.
    if has_long_help {
        print!("{}", HELP_LONG);
        process::exit(0);
    }
    if has_short_help {
        print!("{}", HELP_SHORT);
        process::exit(0);
    }
    if has_version {
        println!("hexyl {}", VERSION);
        process::exit(0);
    }

    if let Err(e) = run(args) {
        eprintln!("{}", e);
        process::exit( get_exit_code(&e) );
    }
}

fn get_exit_code(msg: &str) -> i32 {
    if msg.starts_with("error:") {
        2
    } else if msg.starts_with("Error:") {
        1
    } else {
        1
    }
}

// parsing structures
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Config {
    length: Option<u64>,
    skip: Option<i64>, // may be negative, but after parsing we have signed
    block_size: u64,
    no_squeezing: bool,
    color: String,
    border: String,
    plain: bool,
    no_characters: bool,
    characters: bool,
    character_table: String,
    color_scheme: String,
    no_position: bool,
    display_offset: u64,
    panels: Option<String>, // None or "auto" or number string
    group_size: u8,
    endianness: String,
    use_e_flag: bool,
    base: String,
    terminal_width: Option<u64>,
    print_color_table: bool,
    include: bool,
    completion: Option<String>,
    file: Option<String>,
    // flags for tracking duplicates
    // we need to track if plain already set etc for error handling - done during parse
}

fn run(args: Vec<String>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let cfg = parse_args(args)?;
    if let Some(shell) = cfg.completion {
        print_completion(&shell)?;
        return Ok(());
    }
    if cfg.print_color_table {
        print_color_table();
        return Ok(());
    }
    if cfg.include {
        return run_include(&cfg);
    }
    // otherwise hex viewing
    run_hex(&cfg)
}

fn print_completion(shell: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let out = match shell {
        "bash" => COMPLETION_BASH,
        "fish" => COMPLETION_FISH,
        "zsh" => COMPLETION_ZSH,
        "powershell" => COMPLETION_POWERSHELL,
        "elvish" => COMPLETION_ELVISH,
        _ => return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--completion <SHELL>'\n  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", shell)),
    };
    print!("{}", out);
    Ok(())
}

fn print_color_table() {
    println!("hexyl color reference:");
    println!();
    println!("\x1b[90m⋄ NULL bytes (0x00)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[36ma ASCII printable characters (0x20 - 0x7E)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[32m_ ASCII whitespace (0x09 - 0x0D, 0x20)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[32m• ASCII control characters (except NULL and whitespace)\x1b[39m");
    println!("\x1b[33m× Non-ASCII bytes (0x80 - 0xFF)\x1b[39m");
}

fn parse_args(args: Vec<String>) -> Result<Config, String> {
    let mut cfg = Config {
        length: None,
        skip: None,
        block_size: 512,
        no_squeezing: false,
        color: "always".to_string(),
        border: "unicode".to_string(),
        plain: false,
        no_characters: false,
        characters: false,
        character_table: "default".to_string(),
        color_scheme: "default".to_string(),
        no_position: false,
        display_offset: 0,
        panels: None,
        group_size: 1,
        endianness: "big".to_string(),
        use_e_flag: false,
        base: "hexadecimal".to_string(),
        terminal_width: None,
        print_color_table: false,
        include: false,
        completion: None,
        file: None,
        // ...
    };
    // Track which args have been set for duplicate detection
    let mut seen_length = false;
    let mut seen_skip = false;
    let mut seen_block_size = false;
    let mut seen_no_squeezing = false;
    let mut seen_color = false;
    let mut seen_border = false;
    let mut seen_plain = false;
    let mut seen_no_characters = false;
    let mut seen_characters = false;
    let mut seen_character_table = false;
    let mut seen_color_scheme = false;
    let mut seen_no_position = false;
    let mut seen_display_offset = false;
    let mut seen_panels = false;
    let mut seen_group_size = false;
    let mut seen_endianness = false;
    let mut seen_base = false;
    let mut seen_terminal_width = false;
    let mut seen_print_color_table = false;
    let mut seen_include = false;
    let mut seen_completion = false;

    let mut i = 1;
    let n = args.len();
    let mut positional: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    while i < n {
        let arg = &args[i];
        if arg == "--" {
            // everything after is positional
            for j in i+1..n {
                positional.push(args[j].clone());
            }
            break;
        } else if arg.starts_with("--") {
            // long option
            let (key, val_opt) = if let Some(eq_pos) = arg.find('=') {
                (&arg[..eq_pos], Some(arg[eq_pos+1..].to_string()))
            } else {
                (arg.as_str(), None)
            };
            match key {
                "--length" | "--bytes" => {
                    if seen_length { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--length <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_length = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--length <N>")?;
                    cfg.length = Some(parse_byte_count(&val, cfg.block_size, "--length", false)?);
                }
                "--skip" => {
                    if seen_skip { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--skip <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_skip = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--skip <N>")?;
                    cfg.skip = Some(parse_byte_count_signed(&val, cfg.block_size, "--skip")?);
                }
                "--block-size" => {
                    if seen_block_size { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--block-size <SIZE>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_block_size = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--block-size <SIZE>")?;
                    cfg.block_size = parse_block_size(&val)?;
                }
                "--no-squeezing" => {
                    if seen_no_squeezing { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--no-squeezing' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_no_squeezing = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--no-squeezing' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.no_squeezing = true;
                }
                "--color" => {
                    if seen_color { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--color <WHEN>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_color = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--color <WHEN>")?;
                    if !["always","auto","never","force"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--color <WHEN>'\n  [possible values: always, auto, never, force]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.color = val;
                }
                "--border" => {
                    if seen_border { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--border <STYLE>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_border = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--border <STYLE>")?;
                    if !["unicode","ascii","none"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--border <STYLE>'\n  [possible values: unicode, ascii, none]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.border = val;
                }
                "--plain" => {
                    if seen_plain { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--plain' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_plain = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--plain' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.plain = true;
                }
                "--no-characters" => {
                    if seen_no_characters { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--no-characters' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_no_characters = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--no-characters' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.no_characters = true;
                }
                "--characters" => {
                    if seen_characters { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--characters' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_characters = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--characters' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.characters = true;
                }
                "--character-table" => {
                    if seen_character_table { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--character-table <FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_character_table = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--character-table <FORMAT>")?;
                    if !["default","ascii","codepage-1047","codepage-437","braille"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--character-table <FORMAT>'\n  [possible values: default, ascii, codepage-1047, codepage-437, braille]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.character_table = val;
                }
                "--color-scheme" => {
                    if seen_color_scheme { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--color-scheme <FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_color_scheme = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--color-scheme <FORMAT>")?;
                    if !["default","gradient"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--color-scheme <FORMAT>'\n  [possible values: default, gradient]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.color_scheme = val;
                }
                "--no-position" => {
                    if seen_no_position { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--no-position' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_no_position = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--no-position' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.no_position = true;
                }
                "--display-offset" => {
                    if seen_display_offset { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--display-offset <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_display_offset = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--display-offset <N>")?;
                    cfg.display_offset = parse_byte_count(&val, cfg.block_size, "--display-offset", false)?;
                }
                "--panels" => {
                    if seen_panels { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--panels <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_panels = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--panels <N>")?;
                    if val == "auto" {
                        cfg.panels = Some("auto".to_string());
                    } else {
                        // validate as unsigned nonzero integer
                        match val.parse::<u64>() {
                            Ok(0) => return Err(format!("Error: failed to parse `--panels` arg \"{}\" as unsigned nonzero integer\n\nCaused by:\n    number would be zero for non-zero type\n", val)),
                            Ok(v) => { cfg.panels = Some(v.to_string()); },
                            Err(_) => return Err(format!("Error: failed to parse `--panels` arg \"{}\" as unsigned nonzero integer\n\nCaused by:\n    invalid digit found in string\n", val)),
                        }
                    }
                }
                "--group-size" | "--groupsize" => {
                    if seen_group_size { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--group-size <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_group_size = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--group-size <N>")?;
                    if !["1","2","4","8"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--group-size <N>'\n  [possible values: 1, 2, 4, 8]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.group_size = val.parse().unwrap();
                }
                "--endianness" => {
                    if seen_endianness { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--endianness <FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_endianness = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--endianness <FORMAT>")?;
                    if !["little","big"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--endianness <FORMAT>'\n  [possible values: little, big]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.endianness = val;
                }
                "--base" => {
                    if seen_base { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--base <B>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_base = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--base <B>")?;
                    if !["binary","octal","decimal","hexadecimal"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("Error: The base provided is not valid. Valid bases are \"b\", \"o\", \"d\", and \"x\".\n"));
                    }
                    cfg.base = val;
                }
                "--terminal-width" => {
                    if seen_terminal_width { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--terminal-width <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_terminal_width = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--terminal-width <N>")?;
                    match val.parse::<u64>() {
                        Ok(0) => return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--terminal-width <N>': number would be zero for non-zero type\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val)),
                        Ok(v) => cfg.terminal_width = Some(v),
                        Err(_) => return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--terminal-width <N>': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val)),
                    }
                }
                "--print-color-table" => {
                    if seen_print_color_table { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--print-color-table' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_print_color_table = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--print-color-table' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.print_color_table = true;
                }
                "--include" => {
                    if seen_include { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--include' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_include = true;
                    if val_opt.is_some() { return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '--include' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    cfg.include = true;
                }
                "--completion" => {
                    if seen_completion { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--completion <SHELL>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                    seen_completion = true;
                    let val = get_value(val_opt, &args, &mut i, n, "--completion <SHELL>")?;
                    if !["bash","elvish","fish","powershell","zsh"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                        return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--completion <SHELL>'\n  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                    }
                    cfg.completion = Some(val);
                }
                "--help" | "--version" => {
                    // already handled early, but if reached here via --help=...? not needed
                    unreachable!();
                }
                _ => {
                    return Err(format!("error: unexpected argument '{}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{}' as a value, use '-- {}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", arg, arg, arg));
                }
            }
        } else if arg.starts_with("-") && arg != "-" {
            // short options, may be combined like -vn?
            // We need to support: -n, -c, -l, -s, -v, -p, -C, -P, -o, -g, -e, -b, -i, -h, -V
            // And also -g with value etc.
            // Need to handle combined flags: e.g., -vP ? Not sure if original supports. We'll assume separate only, but also handle combined booleans.
            // For simplicity, if arg starts with single dash and length >2 and second char not expecting value, we treat as combined flags.
            // We'll parse char by char.

            let chars: Vec<char> = arg[1..].chars().collect();
            let mut idx_chars = 0;
            while idx_chars < chars.len() {
                let ch = chars[idx_chars];
                match ch {
                    'n' | 'c' | 'l' => {
                        // length, expects value. If there are remaining chars, they are value? e.g., -n64 or -n=64? But original allows -n 64 and --length=64, but -n64 maybe?
                        // For simplicity, if remaining chars after this char, treat them as value.
                        if seen_length { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--length <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_length = true;
                        let remaining: String = chars[idx_chars+1..].iter().collect();
                        let val = if !remaining.is_empty() {
                            // handle possible '=' prefix? e.g., -n=10? but original may not; but we support
                            if remaining.starts_with('=') { remaining[1..].to_string() } else { remaining }
                        } else {
                            // need next arg
                            if i+1 >= n { return Err(format!("error: a value is required for '--length <N>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                            i+=1;
                            args[i].clone()
                        };
                        cfg.length = Some(parse_byte_count(&val, cfg.block_size, "--length", false)?);
                        break; // consume rest
                    }
                    's' => {
                        if seen_skip { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--skip <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_skip = true;
                        let remaining: String = chars[idx_chars+1..].iter().collect();
                        let val = if !remaining.is_empty() {
                            if remaining.starts_with('=') { remaining[1..].to_string() } else { remaining }
                        } else {
                            if i+1 >= n { return Err(format!("error: a value is required for '--skip <N>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                            i+=1;
                            args[i].clone()
                        };
                        cfg.skip = Some(parse_byte_count_signed(&val, cfg.block_size, "--skip")?);
                        break;
                    }
                    'v' => {
                        if seen_no_squeezing { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--no-squeezing' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_no_squeezing = true;
                        cfg.no_squeezing = true;
                        idx_chars+=1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    'p' => {
                        if seen_plain { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--plain' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_plain = true;
                        cfg.plain = true;
                        idx_chars+=1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    'C' => {
                        if seen_characters { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--characters' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_characters = true;
                        cfg.characters = true;
                        idx_chars+=1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    'P' => {
                        if seen_no_position { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--no-position' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_no_position = true;
                        cfg.no_position = true;
                        idx_chars+=1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    'o' => {
                        if seen_display_offset { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--display-offset <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_display_offset = true;
                        let remaining: String = chars[idx_chars+1..].iter().collect();
                        let val = if !remaining.is_empty() {
                            if remaining.starts_with('=') { remaining[1..].to_string() } else { remaining }
                        } else {
                            if i+1 >= n { return Err(format!("error: a value is required for '--display-offset <N>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                            i+=1;
                            args[i].clone()
                        };
                        cfg.display_offset = parse_byte_count(&val, cfg.block_size, "--display-offset", false)?;
                        break;
                    }
                    'g' => {
                        if seen_group_size { return Err(format!("error: the argument '--group-size <N>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_group_size = true;
                        let remaining: String = chars[idx_chars+1..].iter().collect();
                        let val = if !remaining.is_empty() {
                            if remaining.starts_with('=') { remaining[1..].to_string() } else { remaining }
                        } else {
                            if i+1 >= n { return Err(format!("error: a value is required for '--group-size <N>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                            i+=1;
                            args[i].clone()
                        };
                        if !["1","2","4","8"].contains(&val.as_str()) {
                            return Err(format!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--group-size <N>'\n  [possible values: 1, 2, 4, 8]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", val));
                        }
                        cfg.group_size = val.parse().unwrap();
                        break;
                    }
                    'e' => {
                        // -e is alias for --endianness=little
                        if seen_endianness { return Err(format!("error: the argument '-e' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")); }
                        seen_endianness = true;
                        cfg.endianness = "little".to_string();
                        // also mark use_e_flag? Not needed separate but need to detect duplicate with --endianness
                        // Check if already seen endianness via --endianness, error already handled above? fn parse_byte_count_inner(s: &str, block_size: u64, arg_name: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {

    }
    // Not hex, need to parse integer part + unit.
    // Find where numeric part ends and unit begins.
    // Numeric part is digits 0-9 at start.
    let mut idx = 0;

    while idx < bytes.len() && bytes[idx].is_ascii_digit() {

fn read_input(cfg: &Config) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Option<String>), String> {
    // returns data vector and optional filename (if file source)
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    let mut file_opt: Option<String> = None;
    let mut file_len: Option<u64> = None;

    if let Some(fname) = &cfg.file {
        // open file
        let mut file = File::open(fname).map_err(|e| format!("Error: {} (os error {})", e.to_string(), e.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0)))?;
        // Need file length for negative skip/display offset? But display offset negative not allowed per parse, skip negative handled via seek.
        // For include mode, length already handles limit.
        file_len = file.metadata().ok().map(|m| m.len());
        file_opt = Some(fname.clone());

        // Handle skip
        if let Some(skip_val) = cfg.skip {
            if skip_val >= 0 {
                file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(skip_val as u64)).map_err(|e| format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"))?;
            } else {
                // negative: seek from end
                // skip_val is negative, so -skip_val bytes from end
                let abs = (-skip_val) as u64;
                // Need file len
                if let Some(len) = file_len {
                    if abs > len {
                        return Err(format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"));
                    }
                    file.seek(SeekFrom::End(-(abs as i64))).map_err(|_| format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"))?;
                } else {
                    return Err(format!("Error: Failed to jump to the desired input position. This could be caused by a negative offset that is too large or by an input that is not seek-able (e.g. if the input comes from a pipe).\n"));
                }
            }
        }

        // Now read up to length
        if let Some(len) = cfg.length {
            let mut limited = file.take(len);
            limited.read_to_end(&mut data).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        } else {
            file.read_to_end(&mut data).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        }
    } else {
        // stdin
        let stdin = io::stdin();
        let mut handle = stdin.lock();
        // For stdin, skip handling is different: read and discard
        // If skip is negative, error (since not seekable)
        if let Some(skip_val) = cfg.skip {

        } else {
